analysis.investment_thesis: Equitas SFB is a structurally leveraged microfinance-heavy lender facing an earnings collapse — net profit fell 82% from ₹799 Cr to ₹147 Cr in FY25 — with ROE of 2.42%, which is disqualifying by any serious value investing standard. Finance costs growing at 29.1% CAGR against revenue at 17.4% signals deepening margin compression with no near-term floor visible.
key_strengths: Revenue CAGR of 17.4% over 3 years shows underlying book growth capacity
P/B of 1.28x is modest for a bank, limiting extreme downside
Cash position tripled to ₹5,536 Cr in FY25, providing near-term liquidity buffer
key_risks: Earnings collapsed 82% YoY (₹799 Cr → ₹147 Cr FY25) — microfinance credit stress is severe and ongoing
Finance costs at ₹3,060 Cr now exceed net revenue growth, structurally squeezing profitability
No promoter holding disclosed — Damani's non-negotiable >55% promoter commitment cannot be verified
red_flags: ROE of 2.42% — catastrophically below 15% minimum threshold
Net profit CAGR of -19.4% over 3 years — the opposite of a compounder
Trailing P/E of 50.93x on collapsed earnings — paying growth multiple for a distressed business
Finance cost CAGR of 29.1% vs. revenue CAGR of 17.4% — the spread is moving in the wrong direction
analysis.detailed_analysis:
From my perspective, the first number I look at is ROE — at 2.42%, Equitas SFB is not earning its cost of equity. This is not a temporary dip; it reflects a business that lends to the most stressed segments of the Indian credit market — microfinance and MSME — and is now absorbing the consequences. The 82% profit collapse from FY24 to FY25 (₹799 Cr to ₹147 Cr) while revenue grew 8% tells you the credit cost story is catastrophic. Finance costs compounding at 29.1% while revenue compounds at 17.4% means the business is mathematically destroying value at the operating level.

I have built my portfolio around businesses I can own for 20 years without checking the price. A small finance bank in the microfinance segment, with volatile earnings, no visible promoter anchor, and a balance sheet leveraged beyond my comfort zone, does not qualify. The forward P/E of 11.28x implies the market expects a sharp profit recovery — but I have no way to verify that the credit cycle has turned, and I will not bet on a turnaround in a sector I do not control or deeply understand. I would rather own a boring FMCG company at 25x earnings than a distressed lender at 50x hoping for recovery.
